### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **70** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited), getOverlayRepo (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via applyRegistryWriteThrough (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited), ensureObjectStorage (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaItems (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItemUnaudited))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a8126d244dc46a541b29aafa9bbc543813829f2b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4aeb0b5f13f7b505c496a28517956be5cd854bc2` — the merge of head `6e1d4fe2805a2eb9ca62d52f37a553c446291125` into base `a8126d244dc46a541b29aafa9bbc543813829f2b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4aeb0b5f13f7b505c496a28517956be5cd854bc2 && git checkout 4aeb0b5f13f7b505c496a28517956be5cd854bc2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a8126d244dc46a541b29aafa9bbc543813829f2b 6e1d4fe2805a2eb9ca62d52f37a553c446291125 && git checkout -B drift-repro a8126d244dc46a541b29aafa9bbc543813829f2b && git merge --no-ff 6e1d4fe2805a2eb9ca62d52f37a553c446291125

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a8126d244dc46a541b29aafa9bbc543813829f2b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a8126d244dc46a541b29aafa9bbc543813829f2b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：某个对象装了别的包加进来的扩展字段后，管理员原样再保存这个对象（比如在 Studio 里），以前会被拒绝，提示"会删掉一个字段"；现在可以正常保存。真的删掉对象自己的字段时，照样会被拒。存进去的内容和以前一样，只是判断时把扩展字段也算上了。
- 出错会怎样：最坏的情况是某次本该被拦住的删字段操作被放过。测试两边都钉住了：原样保存放行，真删自己的字段仍然拒绝。
- 要你做什么：不需要。这单的代码没问题，只要把更新说明里的一个标记行从"放宽"改成"否"。这是修回原本承诺的行为，不算放宽公开约定，所以不需要另做一轮契约审核。

## 席位核对 — REWORK (L1-a, declaration line only; the code is accepted) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `16d777ee85082c8dab3ca28fee99ba1051f72fb0` · 2026-11-20T10:29Z

- **Shape** — base `main`, merge-base `65fddc84`, 3 commits: the test first (`b5bfd142`), then the fix (`599f49b4`), then the changeset (`16d777ee`). 3 files, +86/−4.
  - `Fixes #35589`. NOT governed (0 of 3 paths). No contract face is touched (`packages/spec` is untouched, and no schema, rules text or authorable key changes).
- **The fix, read in full** (`protocol-save.ts`, the destructive-change door)
  - `prev` comes from `host.readMetaItem`, which folds every enabled extension onto the owner through `foldObjectExtendersFromRegistry` (`protocol-meta-item-reads.ts:1256/1327`).
  - The fix folds the incoming body through **the same function** (`const next = host.foldObjectExtendersFromRegistry(type, name, request.item)`). So both sides are the served shape, built by one transform, and a contributed column cannot read as a type change from a second fold's shape.
  - `next` replaces `request.item` in exactly three reads: `detectDestructiveObjectChanges(prev, next)`, `withNullMasterRowCounts(…, next, …)` and `withStillShownBy(…, prev, next, …)`.
  - The written body is untouched. The persist path below still reads `request.item`, and the test pins the stored row as `['score', 'title']`, the owner's own layer. The detector is untouched too.
  - Every possible case:
    - an owner-only drop is still `field_removed`, because the fold leaves owner-only keys alone;
    - an owner-only retype is still caught;
    - a column an enabled extension contributes is on both sides, so it is not a drop, which is right because its data stays served;
    - a key the owner drops while an extension still contributes it is not a drop, which is also right.
  - This is the card's "Expected" second form, "the served object minus… / compared served-to-served", in substance.
- **Pins** — `meta-object-extension-item.test.ts`, at the public `PUT /meta/object/NAME?package=` door through the dispatcher:
  - the unchanged re-save answers 200, the stored row holds only the owner's fields, and the served object keeps `leadext_region`;
  - **CONTROL:** dropping the owner's `score` answers 409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` with issues exactly `['field_removed:score']` (the extension's column is not named), and nothing is written.

  The dev's readings, from os-dev-report 7037196825. I did not re-measure them here, because there is no `node_modules`.
  - Reproduced on `main` first: 2 failed, the 409 named `leadext_region`, and the control also named it.
  - After the fix: 52/52.
  - Ablation (`const next = request.item`, with a dist preflight proving it absent): 2 failed, then restored by blob hash.
- **Clause-② — the seat asked me to decide: `no`.** The changeset and the body declare `yes (widening)` because "a save the door refused is now accepted". But `execution-duties.md:111` says 「条款②只指已发布契约面,拉回已声明契约不触它」.
  - The door's declared contract is to refuse a save that **drops** a stored column. ADR-0029 D9.2 makes an enabled extension's column part of the served object, so the 409 was the door breaking its own contract.
  - The fix narrows the refusals back to that contract. It moves no authorable key, schema accept set or published surface.
  - So no L2 is owed. Over-declaring `yes` is not unsafe, but it would buy an L2 this diff does not need.
- **REWORK, one item:** in `.changeset/35589-owner-resave-extension-column.md` and the PR body, change `Clause-②: yes (widening)` to `Clause-②: no`. Leave `Metadata-protocol: none`, and keep the patch level. No code change. I will delta-ACCEPT that head on sight.
- **The two NOT MEASURED families are environment only.**
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` answered exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: 35 dists outside the built closure. CI's Build Core and the dual-build check measure it.
  - `runtime check:test-typecheck` gave TS2307 `Cannot find module '@objectstack/driver-turso'` in three test files this PR does not touch. That is an unbuilt package's declarations missing, and CI's type-check runs with the full build.
  - Neither one reads the changed code.
- **Nit (nothing owed).** When an extension replaces a field under the owner's own key, the diff now judges served type against served type, where before it was owner type against served type. That matches what storage serves. The dev noted it in the PR, and it is not pinned. Acceptable.
- **Gates** — at reading time on this head, CI was still running: Build Core, Type Check, Lint, Check Changeset. The queue guard, PR-body guards, PR size and the dogfood gate are green.
- **Landing terms** — after the declaration fix and my delta ACCEPT on that head, this is not governed and no L2 is owed. The card thread lands with every check green.
